previewNote.en: Change event streaming (CES) is in preview, and vector indexes are a preview feature in SQL Server 2025.

body.en: An embedding is a snapshot of the text at the moment you generated it. When a description is edited, a row is deleted, the chunking rules change or you switch models, stored vectors no longer match reality and search/RAG answers degrade. This lesson covers (1) generating embeddings efficiently and (2) the maintenance methods the study guide lists — **table triggers, Change Tracking, CDC, Azure Functions SQL trigger binding, Azure Logic Apps, change event streaming (CES) and Microsoft Foundry** — and how to choose among them. It builds on the Change Tracking/CDC/CES lesson in Domain 2.

- **In the database**: `AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(text USE MODEL m)` in `UPDATE`/`INSERT … SELECT`, often with `AI_GENERATE_CHUNKS`.
- **Backfill in batches**: process a few hundred rows per statement and commit, instead of one giant transaction (long transactions hold locks and grow the log, and one throttled call can fail everything). Use the model's `retry_count`, pace batches, and stay within your deployment's quota.
- **In the application**: generate with the OpenAI/Azure OpenAI SDK and write with `Microsoft.Data.SqlClient` 6.1+ (`SqlVector<float>` sends vectors in binary); older drivers send JSON strings.
- **Track state**: store the model/version and a hash of the embedded text (e.g., `HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', text)`) so you re-embed only when text really changed, and can find stale rows.

sections.code:
WHILE 1 = 1
BEGIN
    UPDATE TOP (500) e
    SET    e.Embedding = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(p.Description USE MODEL ProductEmbedder),
           e.TextHash  = HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', p.Description),
           e.ModelVersion = 'text-embedding-3-small'
    FROM   dbo.ProductEmbeddings AS e
    JOIN   dbo.Products AS p ON p.ProductId = e.ProductId
    WHERE  e.Embedding IS NULL;

    IF @@ROWCOUNT = 0 BREAK;
END;

body.en:
- **Table triggers** run inside the writing transaction: fastest freshness, but they add work to every write. Calling the model synchronously in a trigger adds network latency, holds locks and can fail the user's write when the endpoint is slow or down — acceptable for prototypes or low-volume tables. A safer pattern: the trigger only **marks** rows (queue table/flag) and a background process embeds them.
- **Change Tracking**: records *which* rows changed; a scheduled job (Elastic Jobs, SQL Agent, an app or Function timer) reads `CHANGETABLE(CHANGES …)` since the last version and re-embeds in batches — a balance of latency and load. Use `TRACK_COLUMNS_UPDATED` with `CHANGE_TRACKING_IS_COLUMN_IN_MASK` (or a text hash) to skip changes that don't touch embedded columns. Retention must exceed the longest possible job outage.
- **CDC**: log-based and asynchronous, with before/after values — suits high-volume tables and lets you compare old vs new text before re-embedding.

- **Azure Functions with SQL trigger binding** (built on Change Tracking): your function receives `SqlChange<T>` batches and calls the embedding API outside the engine, scaling independently. **Beware loops**: if the function writes the embedding back into the *same tracked table*, that update is itself a change. Write to a separate embeddings table, or skip rows whose text hash didn't change.
- **Azure Logic Apps**: low-code orchestration — SQL connector triggers (created/modified) or a recurrence that queries changed rows, an action that calls the embedding endpoint, and an action that writes back; easy to combine with approvals and other systems.
- **Change event streaming (CES)**: streams DML events to Event Hubs/Fabric Eventstream in near real time without extra work in the transaction; consumers (e.g., a Function with an Event Hubs trigger) regenerate embeddings, and several consumers can share the stream. CES doesn't snapshot existing rows (backfill separately) and skips some types, including `vector`.
- **Microsoft Foundry**: manages, evaluates and hosts the embedding models (deployments, versions, quotas). It typically pairs with one of the change-detection methods above; it centralizes model management rather than detecting changes itself.

sections.code:
-- Change Tracking-driven refresh (runs every few minutes)
DECLARE @last BIGINT = (SELECT LastVersion FROM dbo.EmbeddingSync WHERE TableName = 'Products');
DECLARE @now  BIGINT = CHANGE_TRACKING_CURRENT_VERSION();

MERGE dbo.ProductEmbeddings AS e
USING (SELECT ct.ProductId, ct.SYS_CHANGE_OPERATION AS op, p.Description
       FROM CHANGETABLE(CHANGES dbo.Products, @last) AS ct
       LEFT JOIN dbo.Products AS p ON p.ProductId = ct.ProductId) AS s
ON e.ProductId = s.ProductId
WHEN MATCHED AND s.op = 'D' THEN DELETE
WHEN MATCHED AND e.TextHash <> HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', s.Description) THEN
    UPDATE SET Embedding = AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(s.Description USE MODEL ProductEmbedder),
               TextHash  = HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', s.Description)
WHEN NOT MATCHED AND s.op <> 'D' THEN
    INSERT (ProductId, Embedding, TextHash)
    VALUES (s.ProductId, AI_GENERATE_EMBEDDINGS(s.Description USE MODEL ProductEmbedder),
            HASHBYTES('SHA2_256', s.Description));

UPDATE dbo.EmbeddingSync SET LastVersion = @now WHERE TableName = 'Products';

examTips.en: Generation isn't one-time: re-embed on text changes, deletes, chunking changes and model changes.
Backfill in batches with commits; use retry_count and respect quotas.
Triggers = immediate but add work to writes; avoid synchronous model calls in high-volume triggers (mark-and-process instead).
Change Tracking = which rows changed, batch job, balanced; CDC = before/after values, async, high volume.
Functions SQL trigger = Change Tracking + code outside the engine; don't write embeddings back into the tracked table (loop).
Logic Apps = low-code orchestration; CES = near-real-time events to Event Hubs, multiple consumers, no extra transaction work.
Microsoft Foundry = model management/evaluation/hosting, paired with a change-detection method.
After replacing most embeddings (new model), drop and recreate the vector index.
